check_value.description: Check a value somebody published against NIST's own record. Give it the value and the time it was said to come from, and it reads that moment back from NIST and says whether they agree. When they do, it also confirms the value sits inside NIST's chain by reading back the value before it, which is what would catch a record altered after the fact.

mock_response.chain_check: This value carries the value published a minute before it, and that earlier value matches NIST's record, so it sits inside the published chain.

draw_from_list.description: Draw entries out of a list using a random value NIST published, so the result can be checked by anybody rather than trusted. Pick winners of a prize draw, choose which orders to audit, or settle a tie. Each entry can be drawn only once. The answer carries the value used, where to read it on NIST's site, and the arithmetic in one sentence, which together are enough for someone else to arrive at the same picks from the same list.
draw_from_list.display_str_template: Draw {1} from {0} using a value published by NIST.

mock_response.how_it_was_drawn: NIST's published value and the draw's position (0 for the first pick, 1 for the second, and so on) are joined and hashed with SHA-512. The result, read as one long number, is divided by how many entries are still in the list, and the remainder is the position of the entry drawn. That entry is taken out and the next pick repeats on what is left.

description: Use the random values the US National Institute of Standards and Technology publishes, so a random choice can be proved rather than trusted. NIST publishes a fresh 512 bit value every minute, signs it, and leaves it on the public record forever, where anyone in the world can look it up. Announce in advance which minute's value a draw will use, then draw winners, audit samples or tie-breaks from it and hand out the link that lets anybody repeat the same draw and get the same answer. Read the value for any minute since July 2018, list a run of them for an audit trail, and check a value somebody published against NIST's own record. No account, no API key, no sign-up.
